Data Center Market Report – LLNL-TR-2013901 5 Data center cooling technologies are an area for innovation as the data center market scales up [10]. Liquid cooling of computing hardware offers greater efficiency than traditional air cooling and is expected to see substantial growth by 2025 [6]. Cooling systems currently account for up to 40% of a data center’s power usage. This highlights the need for more energy-efficient compute cooling solutions [11]. Innovations in liquid cooling could significantly reduce power consumption and help overcome the critical bottleneck of energy usage in data center operations. U.S. Government Investment in Data Center Infrastructure The U.S. government has demonstrated sustained interest and support for the data center infrastructure development. In 2022, ARPA-E launched the COOLERCHIPS program to reduce cooling energy expenditure to less than 5% of an average data center’s IT load—the total electricity consumed by servers, storage, and network devices [11] [12]. In 2023, the Department of Energy announced $40 million in funding for the program [13]. COOLERCHIPS is now supporting 19 projects focused on improving data center cooling efficiency [11]. Beyond investment in cooling efficiency, the current administration has prioritized large- scale investments in data center infrastructure to support emerging technologies like AI. Prior to taking office, President Trump announced a $20 billion investment by Damac Properties to build data centers in the United States [14]. In late January 2025, Stargate— a $100 billion public-private joint venture—was announced with a goal to build 20 data centers across the U.S., aimed at bolstering domestic AI capabilities [15] [16]. Data Center Market Report – LLNL-TR-2013901 6 Optimizing Data Centers: Livermore's Grid Modeling and Cooling Solutions Key Livermore Technology: Grid Modeling for Future-Proofing Data Centers LLNL POC: Jean-Paul Watson “Builders that optimize site selection can secure prime locations, reduce construction timelines, and integrate operational feedback early, ensuring faster deployment and higher data center efficiency.”- McKinsey.com [1] LLNL’s deep expertise in grid modeling and optimization can guide data center developers toward sites that deliver power reliability and operational economy. Because ensuring a safe, dependable power grid is a matter of national security, Livermore has honed these capabilities for years. Its researchers play leading roles in high-profile efforts such as the Office of Electricity’s Advanced Grid Modeling program [17] and the multi-lab Exascale Computing Project devoted to large-scale grid optimization [18]. LLNL’s unique and powerful grid modeling capability is an integrated grid modeling framework based on mpi-sppy © 2024 for generation and transmission expansion planning modeling [19]. The grid modeling framework co-optimizes generation, transmission and storage investments to deliver cost savings while also significantly enhancing power resilience.
